changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/4730-retire-dead-locale-key-batch.md`

- names `ObjectGrid.tsx` → `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - **Superseded twin vocabularies.** `cellRender.*` and `rowAction.*` duplicated a `grid.*` vocabulary that won. `RowActionMenu.tsx` is fully i18n-wired and reads `grid.openMenu` / `grid.edit` / `grid.delete`; `ObjectGrid.tsx` reads `grid.empty` / `grid.yes` / `grid.no` / `grid.systemFields`. The twins had no reader on either side. - **Labels that outlived their control.** `calendar.agenda` labelled a view mode objectui#5740 retired from `CalendarViewMode` (now `'month' | 'week' | 'day'`). `home.quickActions.createApp*`, `layout.systemNav.createApp`, `actionDialog.defaultActionTitle` / `.ok` and `grid.bulk.selectPlaceholder` sit in namespaces whose consumers are live and wired but demonstrably read other siblings. - **Surfaces that left the product.** `map.*` is the strongest form: `@object-ui/plugin-map` declares no `@object-ui/i18n` dependency and contains no `t()` call at all, so it cannot consume a locale string. `home.stats.*` and `recordDetail.viewersTooltip` name surfaces nothing renders.

### `.changeset/6597-retire-fieldmeta-referenceto.md`

- names `plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx` → `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **No authoring story survived the search either.** `ObjectGrid`'s own relational-meta pass-through (`applyRelationalMeta`, `plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx`) copies `reference_to` / `reference` / `display_field` / etc. from the SCHEMA field def only, at all three of its call sites — never from an authored column override. No doc, example, or fixture in this repo shows a table column pinning a lookup's target away from what its schema field already says. Under the maintainer's standing startup-stage rule (2026-08-27: deprecated/alias spellings retire immediately, no transition windows), no measured demand selects withdraw.

### `.changeset/7762-object-grid-export-options-bare-array-refusal.md`

- names `ObjectGrid.tsx` → `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **What was measured, on this branch's base.** The mirror declared NO `exportOptions` member at all, and `BaseSchema` is `.passthrough()`, so `ObjectGridSchema.safeParse({ type: 'object-grid', objectName: 'accounts', exportOptions: ['csv', 'xlsx'] })` returned `success: true` with the array back VERBATIM — as did `{ formats: ['csv', 'pdf'], compression: 'gzip' }`. Nothing on the render path parses, and `ObjectGrid.tsx` reads `schema.exportOptions?.formats` and only that, so the authored array then lost SILENTLY to the `['csv', 'json']` default: the `useEffect` that warns about dropped formats reads `.formats` too and returns early when it is absent, while `!!schema.exportOptions` kept the export button on screen. An author declared `['csv', 'xlsx']` and got csv/json with no error, no warning and no console line. The two authoring faces disagreed in the direction opposite to objectui#6956's: the TypeScript interface already declared the object form only, so TS refused what zod admitted.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a claim that was born false (a changeset this change adds is excluded by construction), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `2dbb49975` (merge-base with origin/main): 3 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1131 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1643 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/35276811209)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `04f7df346d86f3ba16e2de3541891c4415917e57`

Isolated at-tier review: fed the card (objectui#9722, every comment), the governing ruling (objectui#9511, `Ruling: batch #136 item 5 · letter B`, maintainer-adopted) and this PR only. Every number below was re-measured on a detached worktree at the head above with the dependency `dist`s built, plus the published `@object-ui/plugin-grid@17.6.0` tarball; no repository file was edited. Angle brackets are spelled out on purpose.

### ① Derived judgments

**J1 — the moved face, `BulkExecutorOptions['dataSource']`: a strict RELAXATION for implementors, a narrowing for callers, and both are correct.** Domain: a scratch `tsc` program (same `strict`/`bundler` options as the package) over the head executor and the built `@object-ui/types`; predicate: assignability, each expectation self-checked by a `@ts-expect-error` that reddens as TS2578 if it does not fire; control file lit both directions (TS2578 on an unused directive, TS2322 on an unguarded error). Readings, one run, exit 0: the real `DataSource` is NOT assignable to the base face (the card's rot, R1) and IS assignable to the head face (R2); every value the old face accepted the new face accepts (D1) and not the converse (D2); an implementor whose bulk doors take only strings was refused and is now accepted (I1), one taking the union was and still is accepted (I2); the two doors are identical to `DataSource['bulkUpdate']` / `['bulkDelete']` and the old ones were not (K1–K3); a caller through the face may no longer pass a numeric id (C1). `patch` moves from `Record` of string to unknown to `Partial` of any — subsumed in D1/D2, same direction. The executor's only call sites hand both doors a `string[]` (lines 278–302), so the narrowing on the caller side costs nothing. **Judged correct.**

**J2 — is it a PUBLISHED accept set? No. The `Clause-②: yes` declaration is the prescribed conservative arm, not a fact about the contract.** Measured on the published 17.6.0 bytes, not a local build: `files` ships `dist` and `dist/hooks/useBulkExecutor.d.ts` + `dist/components/BulkActionDialog.d.ts` exist; the `exports` map addresses only `.`; a closure walk of `dist/index.d.ts` over relative imports reaches 18 declaration files and neither of those two — lit member `ObjectGrid.d.ts` and `components/BulkActionBar.d.ts` ARE in the closure, absent probe not; the entry file scores 0 / 0 / 0 for `BulkExecutorOptions` / `useBulkExecutor` / `BulkActionDialog` against a lit 3 for `ObjectGridComponentProps` and 0 for a nonsense token, same file; `dist/ObjectGrid.d.ts` references neither. In-tree consumers outside `packages/plugin-grid`: 0 files for `useBulkExecutor` and `BulkExecutorOptions`, and the 2 non-comment hits for `BulkActionDialog` are both string literals — lit 9 / 13 / 5 files inside the package, absent 0. Contract reading: the `exports` map IS the package's declaration of what it publishes; a declaration file it does not address and the entry's type graph does not reach is shipped bytes, not a public surface — the one route to it is legacy `node10` resolution that ignores `exports`, which is outside the package's declared contract by construction and which this repo does not use (`moduleResolution: bundler`). What follows: nothing on a published surface moves; this review is the whole cost of the `yes`; the declaration stands as filed and is NOT to be re-posted as `no` (that would need a `Contract-text:` citation and a gate re-run and buys this PR nothing); the general question — whether an entry-unreachable, exports-unaddressed d.ts ever counts — is the card the dispatching seat promised, and this record is the contract-side reading for it. Even on the opposite reading, J1 shows the direction is a relaxation, so no published accept set narrows either way.

**J3 — `ObjectGrid` → `BulkActionDialog` hand-off, `as any` → `!`: correct, and the hand-off is a live check again.** Scratch probe over `ComponentProps` of the head dialog: a whole `DataSource` is assignable with no cast (H1); plain `DataSource | undefined` is refused and `!` is accepted (H2) — the assertion erases exactly the optional arm and nothing else, and `!` is erased at runtime, so behaviour is unchanged.

**J4 — `ObjectGrid` → `RecordDetailPanel` hand-off, cast removed: correct, and the card's table was wrong to list it as a bulk-door site.** `RecordDetailPanelProps.dataSource` is `DataSource | undefined` from `@object-ui/types` (read in `@object-ui/plugin-detail`), the same as the grid's prop; `DataSource | undefined` assigns (H3) and a string mutant at that slot reddens (H4, lit). The PR's correction of the card is right.

**J5 — nothing contradicts objectui#9511 ruling B.** `packages/types/src/data.ts` is byte-identical base..head (`git diff --quiet` exit 0); both `DataSource` bulk doors still refuse a numeric id (B1, B1b). The repair narrows the CONSUMER to the ruling; it re-widens nothing on the boundary, and neither refused letter (A: leave doors wide; C: revert) is re-run. `findOne` remains `string | number` on `DataSource` — deliberately held open by the ruling's own follow-up, untouched here.

**J6 — `update` / `delete` kept spelled out: the stated reason holds.** `Pick` of the four members refuses a double whose `delete` resolves `Promise` of unknown while the head face accepts it (P1 / P2). Their text is unchanged, so no Clause-② move in either direction.

**J7 — scope: exactly the card, nothing more.** 4 files: the executor face + its docblock (the "without importing it" claim was false — `DataSource` was already imported in this file — and correcting it belongs to the face repair), two JSX prop values in `ObjectGrid.tsx` (`dataSource={dataSource as any}` reads 2 at base, 0 at head; the rest of that file's hunks are comments), the new pin, the changeset.

**J8 — the PR's measurements are sound.** Every zero in the body carries a lit control on the same instrument and corpus (reachability 0/0/0 vs 3; out-of-package 0 vs 17 files; the RecordDetailPanel cast's zero errors vs a TS2322 at the same address). Blob hashes and byte counts are real: base `ObjectGrid.tsx` is 296938 bytes at blob `faa5a1b8…`, head `useBulkExecutor.ts` is blob `9d18c09d…`, both as the body states; the cited addresses `(5352,7)` and `(4728,13)` are the two hand-off lines at head with the column matching the indentation. The ablation discipline is stated correctly (mutation proven by blob + byte delta before reading, restoration by blob equality + empty `git diff HEAD`), its six-way redden is what the pin's rows predict (two identity rows, one whole-adapter row, two directives going unused, the hand-off) and its 2-of-9 vitest failures are the two census rows. Re-run here without mutation: `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/plugin-grid` exit 0 with the dependency builds; the pin file 9 / 9 under vitest; `check-changeset-presence` and `check-changeset-no-major` exit 0; CI on this head 33 success, 3 skipped, 0 non-green of 36.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@object-ui/plugin-grid`, consistent with the declared widening: an enlarged accept set is additive, which is `minor`, and AGENTS.md forbids only `major`. On J2 the honest floor is `patch` (no published surface moves), but `minor` is not wrong and is inert in practice — the fixed group already carries hundreds of pending `minor` entries, so the released level is unchanged either way. Declaration and changeset agree; no change required.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Security / permissions:** none. No key becomes writable, no runtime path changes, no wire bytes move.
- **Gate strength:** up, not down — the hand-off is a real check (J3), and the pin refuses both retired spellings from a scoped slice with a quotation control that proves the slice is narrower than the file.
- **Open question 1 (Clause-②):** answered at J2 — not a published accept set; the declaration stands as the conservative arm; the precedent question needs its own card.
- **Open question 2 (claim legibility):** moot — `check-clause2-carriers --pair 9732` read exit 0 (both carriers agree) before this record was posted.
- **Noted, not filed — agreed with the implementer:** (a) the optionality gap (grid `dataSource?` vs executor demanding one) is pre-existing and reachable only if a grid with no data source can open the bulk dialog; the `!` neither creates nor worsens it; (b) the neighbouring `objectSchema as any` is a separate question, untouched.
- **One further note for the seat that closes `findOne`:** `BulkActionDialogProps.dataSource` still RESTATES `findOne` with `id: string | number`. That is correct today because `DataSource.findOne` is held open by objectui#9511's follow-up — but it is the same restatement class as this card, and it will rot the day `findOne` narrows unless it is derived then. Not this PR's.
- **Independence:** `Implemented-by` is the branch (mode:subagent); `Reviewed-by` is the adopting seat's session, which the implementation claim also names — the in-seat compensating design the reference describes. This record was rendered by an isolated review sub-agent fed the card, the ruling and the PR only.
